units.title: Couple the initial and reference phase laws with identical momentum
units.boundary: This is only the q=2 coupling-cost edge in the proof of SPHMC Lemma 4.16. It does not yet insert Gibbs concentration or the small-gradient reference-point bound, establish q>2, or control any Picard trajectory.

sources.label: Smoothed Picard Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, Lemma 4.16 proof
sources.scope: ASTIS expands the source's identical-momentum coupling and the precise Kantorovich-cost estimate.

assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space.
The target position law pi is a probability measure with an integrable squared distance from xref.
The paper phase parameter kappa is at least one; its M_kappa quadratic form is used without changing normalization.
Both phase laws use the same standard-Gaussian momentum marginal.
units.statement: The actual initial phase law at xref and any product reference law with standard-Gaussian momentum admit a coupling that uses the same momentum on both sides. Its M-kappa transportation cost is at most the reference law's position second moment about xref.

steps.title: Build the actual coupling
steps.text: Draw Y from pi and P independently from the standard Gaussian; pair the phase states (xref,P) and (Y,P). The first and second marginals are exactly the required phase laws.
steps.lean: identicalMomentumCoupling; Measure.fst_map_prodMk, Measure.snd_map_prodMk and Measure.dirac_prod certify both marginals.

steps.title: Cancel the momentum displacement
steps.text: For a paired sample the momentum difference is zero. The paper's twisted quadratic form therefore reduces to its position coefficient, which is at most one when kappa is at least one.
steps.lean: phaseCost_identical_momentum_le unfolds the exact phase cost and proves the coefficient inequality.

steps.title: Bound the Kantorovich infimum
steps.text: Any admissible coupling upper-bounds the optimal transport cost. Measurability permits pushforward integration, and the finite position moment converts the nonnegative Lebesgue integral back to the ordinary expectation.

units.lean_statement: The result controls the squared Kantorovich value directly. It is generic in the position law, so the paper's smoothed Gibbs law must still be supplied by a separate specialization.
units.lean_proof: The proof constructs an explicit pushforward coupling; it does not assume existence of an optimal coupling. Product-law measurability and square integrability justify the cost calculation.
